site_or_subject: Registration of virtual currency mining facilities as large flexible loads (SB 1929, PURA §39.360; 16 TAC §25.114)
record: SB 1929 (88th Legislature, effective September 1, 2023) added PURA 'Sec. 39.360. LARGE FLEXIBLE LOAD REGISTRATION', requiring operators of virtual currency mining facilities taking retail service in the ERCOT region to register when 'the facility requires a total load of more than 75 megawatts' and 'the facility load is interruptible', including location and anticipated demand over five years (Senate bill analysis). The PUCT implemented it in Project No. 56962 as 16 TAC §25.114 (proposed in the Texas Register of 13 September 2024; order adopting signed November 2024). The rule applies where total load exceeds 75 MW and the 'interruptible load equals 10 percent or more of the actual or anticipated annual peak demand'; facilities already in service had to 'register no later than February 1, 2025'. The adoption order states registration information 'will be collected via an internal-facing online tool that will not be accessible to the public.' The PUCT's virtual currency mining web page describes the requirement and lists no registered facilities.

site_or_subject: ERCOT large-load interconnection: approved and observed large-load MW, and the 2026 pause on energizing data centers and virtual currency mining facilities
record: ERCOT's Large Load Interconnection Status Update (6 Sept 2024) reports 'Of the total 5,496 MW Approved to Energize' (4,421 MW standalone, 1,075 MW co-located), an observed 'nonsimultaneous peak consumption of 3,282 MW' and a 'simultaneous peak consumption of 2,815 MW'; it splits load by zone and standalone/co-located, not by crypto mining. ERCOT's 20 Aug 2026 presentation to the PUCT open meeting states that on 3 Aug 2026 ERCOT issued a Market Notice and 'Paused approvals to energize data centers or virtual currency mining facilities' of 75 MW or greater, following the Governor's directive for 'a comprehensive verification and audit', and that ERCOT 'will request information from data center and crypto facilities that have requested 25 MW or more'; a Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report is due 10 December 2026. ERCOT's Batch Zero Update to its Board (14-15 Sept 2026) lists '204 projects (66.4 GW)' conditionally included as base load and '158 projects (127.9 GW)' as studied load, with no crypto breakout. Texas RE (Nov 2025) states 'Data centers and crypto mining facilities account for over 80 percent of the interconnection requests'. EIA (3 Oct 2024) reported ERCOT large flexible load (LFL: crypto mining, data centers, some industrial) approvals of 5,479 MW and that 'LFL customers have consumed about 65% of their total approved capacity.' ERCOT's Dec 2022 CEO update lists 'Operational co-located resources with LFLs: 2,996 MW'.

site_or_subject: Moratorium on air permits for carbon-fuel power plants supplying behind-the-meter power to cryptocurrency mining (ECL §19-0331; Chapter 628 of the Laws of 2022)
operator: New York State Legislature; New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
record: Bill A7389C (passed Assembly 26 April 2022; passed Senate 2 June 2022, substituted for S6486D) adds ECL §19-0331, 'MORATORIUM ON AIR PERMIT ISSUANCE AND RENEWAL': 'FOR THE PERIOD COMMENCING ON THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF THIS SECTION AND ENDING TWO YEARS AFTER SUCH DATE' the department 'SHALL NOT APPROVE A NEW APPLICATION FOR OR ISSUE A NEW PERMIT' for 'AN ELECTRIC GENERATING FACILITY THAT UTILIZES A CARBON-BASED FUEL AND THAT PROVIDES, IN WHOLE OR IN PART,' 'BEHIND-THE-METER ELECTRIC ENERGY CONSUMED OR UTILIZED BY CRYPTOCURRENCY MINING OPERATIONS', and shall not approve renewals that would 'INCREASE' the electric energy so used; DEC must issue a final generic environmental impact statement 'no later than one year after the effective date of this act.' DEC's April 2024 final GEIS scope cites 'Chapter 628 of the Laws of 2022' and states 'This law also established a two-year moratorium on the issuance of certain permits to certain cryptocurrency mining operations.' DEC's Environmental Notice Bulletin of 28 May 2025 announced a draft GEIS on 'cryptocurrency mining operations that use proof-of-work authentication methods', with comments accepted 'until September 25, 2025'.

site_or_subject: EIA Form EIA-862, Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities Report (2024 emergency survey)
record: On February 23, 2024 the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, Waco Division (No. 6:24-cv-00099-ADA; Texas Blockchain Council and Riot Platforms, Inc. v. Department of Energy, EIA, OMB et al.) issued a temporary restraining order: the defendants are 'restrained from requiring Plaintiffs or their members to respond to the Survey', 'restrained from collecting data required by the Survey', and 'shall sequester and not share any such data that Defendants have already received from Survey respondents.' EIA's February 1, 2024 analysis page carries the notice: 'EIA has discontinued the emergency collection of data for Form EIA-862, Cryptocurrency Mining Operations Survey.'
